name: Content Writer
description: AI-powered long-form content generation. Writes content using analysis (required), optional SEO plan (keyword distribution), and scraped source content (raw material for specific details). Produces markdown output. Requires content-analyzer; seo-planner is optional.
usage_notes: Requires content-analyzer. seo-planner is optional — if absent, writer warns and proceeds without SEO plan section. Use sonnet for production-quality content; haiku produces acceptable drafts. Increase max_source_chars for entities with extensive source material.

options.name: ai_model
options.label: AI Model
options.description: Which model to use for content writing. Larger models produce better prose.

options.name: reference_docs
options.label: Reference Documents
options.description: Reference docs for writing. Key docs: tone_guide.md (voice rules, citation format), format_spec.md (section structure, word counts). style_examples.md optional for few-shot quality.

options.name: temperature
options.label: Temperature
options.description: LLM temperature for writing. Higher = more creative prose. Default 0.4 balances quality with consistency.

options.name: max_tokens
options.label: Max output tokens
options.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM response. Without this, long articles silently truncate. Default 16384 for full company profiles.

options.name: max_source_chars
options.label: Max source content characters
options.description: Truncate scraped source text to this many characters to control token usage.

options.name: requires_prompt_override
options.label: Requires Prompt Override (per-template)
options.description: If true and the prompt at runtime equals the manifest default (no template override configured), content-writer refuses the run early with a clear error. Default false (the manifest default is a valid generic run path). Templates that depend on pipeline-specific output shape (e.g. company-profile bracket-heading format, news-article lede/quotes structure, podcast episode summary) should set this true and configure a prompt override so a missing override fails loud instead of silently producing an unexpectedly generic article.

options.name: allowed_slug_paths
options.label: Allowed slug paths (per-template closed vocabulary)
options.description:
Optional. When set, the writer extracts per-entity closed-vocabulary slug lists from analysis_json using these paths and prepends an `ALLOWED SLUGS FOR THIS ARTICLE` block to the entity content. The prompt should then instruct the model to draw slug values inside its bracket headings exclusively from that block.

This option is pipeline-agnostic — leave empty for content types that do not use slug brackets in headings (cover letters, news articles, podcast pages, etc.). Templates whose prompt uses brackets like [Category: <slug>] or [Topic: <slug>] populate this to anchor the model against narrative drift.

Format: one entry per line.
    <BracketLabel>=<dot.notation.path>

Syntax: `field.subfield[].leaf` walks an array and pulls each item's `leaf`. Labels may repeat — repeated labels concatenate slug lists. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.

Example for a company-profile pipeline:
    Primary Category=categories.primary[].slug
    Secondary Category=categories.secondary[].slug
    Tag=tags.existing[].slug
    Tag=tags.suggested_new[].label

Example for a news pipeline:
    Topic=topics[].slug
    Mentioned Entity=entities.mentioned[].slug

options.name: prompt
options.label: Writing prompt
options.description: The prompt sent to the AI. Use {entity_content} for analysis+plan+sources data, {doc:filename} for reference doc content.
options.default:
You are a content writer. Produce content based on the structured inputs below.

You do NOT decide what topic to write about — the upstream analyzer step does that. You do NOT decide the section structure or word counts — the format spec (if provided) does that. Your role is to produce well-cited, factual prose that follows decisions already made upstream.

### INPUTS

The block below contains analyzer output, optional SEO plan, and source content. If an `=== ALLOWED SLUGS FOR THIS ARTICLE ===` block appears at the top of the input, those are the only slug values you may use inside bracket markers in your output.

{entity_content}

### RULES

If a format specification is provided, follow it exactly:
{doc:format_spec.md}

If a tone guide is provided, follow it:
{doc:tone_guide.md}

### KEY INSTRUCTIONS

- Draw specific details from the source content. Do not write generic prose that could apply to anything.
- Cite sources inline using [#n] format for every factual claim, mapping to the source_citations from the analyzer output.
- Output markdown only — no JSON, no code fences, no preamble.
- Do not invent facts beyond what the analyzer output contains.
- If the input includes an ALLOWED SLUGS block, every bracket-marker value in your output must come from that block. Do not paraphrase or invent slug values.
